thesis: Eaton is the highest-quality large-cap way to own data center electrification, selling the switchgear, busway, UPS, medium-voltage gear, modular power skids and (post-Boyd) liquid cooling that sit between the utility and the chip. Q2 2026 was a record: revenue $8.53B (+21% total, +14% organic), adjusted EPS $3.15, and data center organic revenue up ~65% against an underlying market growing 23%. Rolling 12-month orders are up 41% in Electrical Americas and 33% in Electrical Global, total Electrical backlog is up 43% YoY, and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.40–$13.60. The offsets are valuation (~32x FY2026 adjusted EPS, 44x trailing GAAP), a balance sheet that carried $21.3B of debt and only $695M of cash after ~$11B of Q1 acquisitions, and the fact that Electrical Americas margins are still below prior-year levels while the capacity ramp works through price/cost.

drivers: Data center orders keep compounding: 307 GW of announced US data center backlog is ~15 years of build at 2025 rates, with only ~20% converting near term and the bulk landing 2028+
Electrical Americas margins reach the 2030 target of 32% as price/cost turns neutral and the two dozen capacity projects hit full productivity
Boyd Thermal scales past the raised $1.8B FY2026 revenue plan and joins the organic base in 2027, making Eaton a grid-to-chip supplier with cold plates and CDUs
The 800-volt DC transition raises content per megawatt above the current ~$3.4M, with Resilient Power solid-state transformers as a differentiator
Mobility exits via the Dana RMT in Q1 2027, leaving a higher-growth, higher-margin Electrical plus Aerospace company that re-rates on mix

base_case.assumptions: FY2026 lands near the guided midpoint of 12% organic growth and $13.50 adjusted EPS, with Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.46–$3.56 and segment margins of 24.6–25.0%. FY2027 adjusted EPS reaches roughly $15 on low-double-digit organic growth plus the Boyd and COL contributions, and the stock holds ~31–34x forward adjusted earnings. This range brackets the S&P Global consensus target of ~$480.

risks: Hyperscaler capex digestion: orders decelerate from a 1.3 book-to-bill and the 43% backlog growth reverses, compressing the multiple toward 22–24x
Electrical Americas margin recovery slips again — the year-over-year decline was driven by price/cost and the ramp has already disrupted two quarters
$21.3B of total debt against $695M of cash leaves little flexibility if rates stay high and the acquisition pace continues
Tariffs, copper and steel inflation, or supply chain constraints re-open a negative price/cost gap
Dana RMT closing risk or dis-synergies, plus integration risk across Boyd, Ultra PCS, Fibrebond, Resilient Power and COL Group simultaneously

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results; guidance is adjusted EPS of $3.46–$3.56 and segment margin of 24.6–25.0%, the first clean test of the promised 250 bp sequential Electrical Americas margin step-up
Electrical Americas margin exit rate — management guided a further 200–250 bp sequential improvement, of which 150 bp is price/cost

Expected close of the Reverse Morris Trust combining Eaton's Mobility Group with Dana, creating a company valued above $10B with Eaton holders owning at least 50.1%; accretive to Eaton's organic growth and margins on close
Q4 and FY2026 results plus initial FY2027 guidance, including the first full-year framing of a post-Mobility Eaton
Close of the EUR810M COL Group acquisition from Oaktree, adding EMEA medium-voltage distribution capacity for data center and utility customers (signed 2026-09-24)

key_risks: Valuation: ~32x FY2026 guided adjusted EPS and ~44x trailing GAAP EPS leaves no room for a guidance miss
AI capex concentration — data center is the growth engine and hyperscaler spending is discretionary and lumpy
Electrical Americas operating margin fell year over year on negative price/cost; the recovery is guided, not delivered
Leverage: $21.3B total debt and $695M cash at 2026-06-30 after roughly $11B of Q1 2026 acquisitions
Execution risk across five acquisitions being integrated at once plus two dozen in-flight capacity projects
Mobility/Dana RMT is not yet closed; delay or renegotiation would muddy the 2027 growth and margin story
Tariff and commodity cost volatility, and a residential end market that management describes as weak
